correctness.rationale: The normalized midpoints are (u+v)/(2φ) for v·u=φ, with squared length one. On homogeneous degree-ℓ polynomials the tangential gradient in ambient coordinates is ∇H(w)−ℓH(w)w. A fresh reconstruction selects the edges exactly, checks the 30 distinct reduced unit nodes, forms denominator-cleared harmonic bases and reduces via φ→23 in F₁₀₁. Since φ²−φ−1 vanishes at 23 and 2φ is invertible there, the ranks (3,5,7,9,11,12) give characteristic-zero lower bounds by lifting nonzero minors. Degrees 1–5 reach their full dimensions. The sextic is a sum of solid zonal harmonics and is invariant by vertex permutation. Half-turns about the midpoint directions fix the nodes and act as −I on the respective tangent planes, forcing zero tangential gradients. Directly, with q=φ+2, the sums of t_v²,t_v⁴,t_v⁶ at e₁ are 4q, 12q²/5, 8q³/5; hence F₆(e₁)=−132q³/5≠0 (85 mod 101). Thus the degree-six rank is at most 12 independently of reduction; equality and the claimed kernel line follow.
residual_risks: The nonzero modular minors establish lower bounds, not upper bounds; the exact symmetry argument establishes the remaining upper bound. No stability or rank claim is made for higher degrees; degree zero is deliberately excluded.

value.rationale: The orbit is a standard symmetric sampling grid and the observable is natural for derivative-only reconstruction. Despite many more nominal tangent measurements than harmonic dimensions, the first invariant degree has a blind direction. Identifying the full kernel and confirming that earlier degrees really are injective gives a useful exact sampling boundary, stronger than observing symmetry-forced failure at six alone.
residual_risks: Injectivity is not a quantitative condition-number estimate; no universal claim about scattered nodes, mixed jets, or other orbits.
